title: Paper: how does the size of a task relate to its cost?
description:
## The question

John (5 Nov): **how does the "size" of a task, an ambiguous word, relate to its cost?**

A paper for the Library (`docs/papers/harbour/`, under `docs/papers/standard.md`): one question, answered with evidence.

## Why now

The archive has argued this but never measured it in money. `coherence-as-it-grows` found that a change touching a known scattered decision is about five times the size (229 production lines at the median against 45) and sent back more than twice as often (0.56 against 0.23). Within a size band, it takes no more hours and escapes no more often. `the-second-copy` put it as "the size *is* the cost". The measure is partly circular, and "no trend in the cost of a same-sized change has been shown". `tasks-are-tasks` (v5) says the Costs meter "would let it be seen".

As of 4 November the meter exists. Every model request a worker makes is a record, priced and counted once under its lineage and issue (Costs rebuild 2, LIN-4195). Per-issue cost is readable through the proxy: `GET /api/proxy/issues/{identifier}/cost`, which also says what is unpriced. So this is the first time the question can be answered rather than argued.

## "Size" is several things; separate them first

These are starting senses, not a scheme to fill in. The paper may find others, merge them, or drop them.

* **Asked size:** the ticket's breadth. How many surfaces it names, and whether its goal is closed (a check) or open (a judgement).
* **Landed size:** production lines and files changed, and how many pieces or PRs it became.
* **Bound size:** how much the change had to push through or work around to land. How many places held a decision it touched; how many lists, registries, docs or guards had to learn about it; how many areas it crossed. The Survey forecasts (`docs/plans/survey/`), the blind place reads in `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md`, and the builders' after-answers already count these for recent tickets.
* **Proving size:** tests, goldens, censuses and fixtures. Builders keep saying "proving costs more than changing", and test lines often run five to ten times the production lines.

Cost is several things too: **model spend** (tokens and USD per lineage), **wall time**, **send-backs and review or plan-review rounds**, **rulings** (the person's presses), and **later repair** (follow-up fixes, escapes, tidy-afters).

## What to look at

* **The recent record,** where cost is exact: tickets since about 05:00 UTC on 4 November, read by `/cost`. They include the Survey loop's tickets, with their forecasts, at-merge readings and builders' answers in `docs/plans/survey/`.
* **Natural experiments in that window.**
  * Tidy-first pairs: LIN-4253 → LIN-4251, and LIN-4252 → LIN-4246 (with LIN-4255 as LIN-4252's tidy-after). Did a tidy done first move cost out of the follow-on into the tidy, or remove it?
  * A control: LIN-4247, a feature with its tidy folded in.
  * LIN-4201 / LIN-4226: a larger extra mispriced as free, then split off.
* **The longer record,** where cost is approximate: snapshot-era cost, with its known gaps (Haiku unpriced, subagents uncounted), plus hours, send-backs and the coherence census's exposure data.
* **John's Hanoi point (5 Nov):** to move a feature cleanly you first move the tidy, and to move the tidy cleanly you first move its copies. Does cost rise faster than size once a change binds across layers? And does a smaller move still make the next change in that area cheaper ("trending in the right direction, if not the full stack")?

## Cautions

* The exact-cost window is short. Say how many tickets carry each claim. A pair is an anecdote, not a rate.
* Some surfaces are still unpriced or snapshot-only. Use `/cost`'s `unpriced` and coverage fields, and never read an unknown as zero.
* Don't let the paper become the drill by other means: if a sense of size predicts nothing, say so.
* Don't change code, tickets or rulings to make the evidence. This is read-only research; the paper and its evidence files are the only writes.

## Done when

`docs/papers/harbour/<a name the writer chooses>.md`, `kind: paper`, with the Library header, a question for a title, `grounded_at` and citations a reader can land on. It answers the question in its first paragraph, as far as the evidence allows, and says where it doesn't. Evidence files go in a folder beside it if they're needed. Merged through the usual review, with a fresh reader given only the file before merge.

## Report back

The answer in a sentence or two, what the evidence couldn't settle, and what would settle it.

## Implementation Plan (archived)

Implemented as approved, with no deviations to the plan. The paper `docs/papers/harbour/task-size-and-cost.md` (with frozen evidence in `task-size-and-cost-evidence/2026-11-05/` and scripts in `task-size-and-cost-scripts/`) merged in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2294](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2294>) as e4fa8d34. Review's eight text fixes were made at close-out. The `/cost` per-model and token exposure is filed as LIN-4264.

Session fit: fits one session

plan-review due: no

The Survey's "how to go about it", the research findings and the full implementation plan were removed from this description after landing. The full history is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4257 @ b5cc4c621

Code read at `b5cc4c621`; `/cost` read for the named tickets at about 11:40 on 5 Nov.

**Why this will be hard: most of the money isn't size.** On every finished ticket in the window, the fixed legs (plan, plan-review, review, close-out, autopilot and the two survey legs) cost about $5–7, whatever the change. Implementation is a minority of the total: LIN-4247 $0.70 of $6.27 (11%), LIN-4252 $3.03 of $10.38, LIN-4253 $3.85 of $11.24 (about a third). `cost-mix.md` already named a "small-change floor". Correlate any sense of size against the total and you mostly get noise on top of the floor. The Hanoi question in money then becomes: every extra move pays the floor again. A tidy done first doesn't just move cost; it adds about $5–7. The question behind this ticket may really be "what is the floor, and what is the variable cost made of?"

**Three confounds sit inside the meter:**
- **Model choice.** Implementation ran on Opus for LIN-4253, 4252 and 4201 and on Haiku for 4251, 4246, 4247 and 4226. If the route was chosen from how big the ticket looked, implementation USD partly records that guess, which brings back the circularity `the-second-copy` warned about. Compare within one model, or compare tokens, not just dollars.
- **Supervision and waiting.** LIN-4195 is $76, and $67 of it is one autopilot session that ran about 19 h. LIN-4201's `custom` leg is $26 of $40. The big totals measure how long something was kept alive, not how big the change was.
- **The observer is billed.** `survey-task` and `survey-place` legs (about $1.8–2 per ticket; LIN-4246 was surveyed twice, $3.08) are charged to the issue. The exact-cost window is mostly the Survey loop's own tickets, so the measurement is part of what's measured.

**The natural experiments weren't finished at base:**
- LIN-4251: `totalUsd: null`, and its review has no telemetry yet (`noTelemetryCount: 1`).
- LIN-4246: still has no review or close-out legs.
- LIN-4255 (the tidy-after): `noLineage: true`, with no record at all. That's unknown, not $0.

So both tidy-first pairs are incomplete as well as being n=1. The control (LIN-4247) is the only clean one.

**Size sources are uneven.** Bound size is counted only for tickets the Survey touched (the place-ledger and the builders' answers), which is a selected sample. Landed size and proving size need PR diffs split into production and test lines. The window since 05:00 on 4 Nov is about 30 hours, so expect tens of tickets, not hundreds.

**What I'd do first:**
1. Pull `/cost` for every issue in the window into one table, one row per leg: kind, model, USD, duration and completeness flags. Mark unfinished lineages instead of reading them as totals.
2. Split each ticket into **floor** (the planning, review, close-out and survey legs), **work** (implementation) and **keep-alive** (autopilot and custom duration). Report the survey legs separately.
3. Only then attach the size senses, and test them against **work**, within one model.
4. Re-read the pairs after LIN-4251 and LIN-4246 close. Say whether LIN-4255 can be priced at all.

If no sense of size predicts **work** once the floor and the model are taken out, say so. That would be a result too.

## Survey global: LIN-4257 @ b5cc4c621

*LinearViewer `origin/main`. Read-only.*

**Where it lands.** In `docs/papers/harbour/` plus three things that have to hear about it: the index `docs/papers/README.md`, `proposals.md` (Next, at least one line, under `standard.md` rule 3), and a check document later. It is growing in two places. First, each paper keeps its own `*-scripts/` folder, and several already measure "size" separately: `unwedge-or-breakdown-scripts/sizebands.mjs` (insertions plus deletions per LIN id, tests included, using the how-a-task-is-composed bands), `coherence-as-it-grows-scripts/lineage.py` (production lines, which is the 229/45 figure), and `scripts/delivery-composition.mjs`. Second, nothing checks the index: no test reads `docs/papers`, and two files are already missing from it (`fleet-complexity-read.md`, `replay-small-work-preregistration.md`). An omission would go unnoticed.

**Done the obvious way.** The paper would write a fourth size counter and a cost fetcher, each in its own folder. It would also hand-copy the bound-size counts out of `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` and `round-2/3/forecasts.md`, which are prose tables, into a JSON evidence file, leaving them in two places. Things the paper needs to know about the instrument:
- **The meter counts the Survey.** `/cost` on LIN-4247 lists `survey-place` and `survey-task` sessions, about 30% of its $6.27. For the tidy-first pairs, the survey loop's overhead has to be split out by `kind`, or a surveyed tidy looks dearer than an unsurveyed one for reasons unrelated to size.
- **The longer record has an expiry date.** `lib/cost-read.js:109`: the snapshot reader is LEGACY, to be deleted no earlier than 2026-12-04. App-call cost reads a 30-day window (`window.appCallsSince`). Any approximate cost the paper uses must be frozen into its evidence file with the read date, or nobody will be able to re-run its Method after December.
- **Size can't be read from `/cost`.** It has to come from git, and a ticket may land in both repos. `place-change.mjs` only covers LinearViewer (simple-dispatcher has no area guide). So bound size would be unevenly measured across the two repos.
- **The question already has a line.** `proposals.md:81–86` asks for "hours per same-sized change" set against exposure, which is the same question in hours. The PR should replace or answer that line rather than open a parallel one.

**What would leave it better, at this task's cost.** Reuse `sizebands.mjs` and `lineage.py`, by import or invocation, instead of writing a new counter, and say which size each one measures. Store `/cost` readings as dated JSON. Add the paper and the two missing files to the README index. Retire or answer `proposals.md:81`.

**Better, but not this task's to carry.** A shared paper-scripts library for "size of a ticket" and "cost of a ticket", so the next paper doesn't write a fifth counter. A unit test that every `harbour/*.md` with a `kind:` header appears in the index. Machine-readable rows for the place ledger.

**Symptom or cause.** The ticket asks the right question. The deeper issue is that "size" has no single home in this codebase, so every paper redefines it, and that redefinition is itself an example of the scattered decision the paper is studying.

## Research: LIN-4257 @ LinearViewer `b5cc4c62`, simple-dispatcher `07c88f7`

Read-only. `/cost` and dispatch rows read 11:45–12:05 UTC on 5 Nov. Nothing was written except this comment and the description. The spike data sits in my session scratchpad only; it is **not** the frozen evidence (the paper must make its own dated read).

**Staleness check.** `git log --since=2026-11-05T11:36:51Z` is empty in both repos. HEAD is the Surveys' base, so every file the ticket names is as the Surveys read it. Three of the ticket's claims about the code are wrong all the same (corrections 1–3 below).

### Corrections to the ticket and Surveys (each verified)

1. **`lineage.py` is not a size counter.** `coherence-as-it-grows-scripts/lineage.py:1-30` traces four copy-pasted decisions (D1–D4) through history. The 229 vs 45 production-line figure (`coherence-as-it-grows.md:100`) comes from `coherence-census.mjs prs` (`coherence-as-it-grows-scripts/coherence-census.mjs:150-191`, fields `prodAdded/prodDeleted/testAdded/testDeleted/prodFiles/areas`), read by `decision-exposure.py:21,513` and `exposure.py:40`. Reuse `coherence-census.mjs prs`, not `lineage.py`. Its rev argument takes a range (`015aa4c6..origin/main` ran in seconds).
2. **The "model confound" is not what the Survey says.** Every one of the 45 implementation dispatch rows in the window was routed to **Haiku** (`GET /dispatch/{rootItemId}` → `model: claude-haiku-5-5`, all 45). `/cost` labels 21 of those lineages Opus because the label is the lineage's *last counted row* (`lib/cost-read.js:469-477`, "LIN-2830: the labels come from the lineage's last counted row"), and a lineage includes its follow-ups. Of the 21 Opus-labelled implementation lineages:
   - **17** carry an Opus `custom` follow-up whose prompt begins "A short, read-only follow-up for research (the Survey…)" ("Survey 1a (round 3)", the builder's after-answer, resumed into the build session after merge): LIN-4048, 4143, 4151, 4177, 4178, 4179, 4196 (root 67b95877), 4201, 4234, 4239, 4240, 4241, 4242, 4243, 4248, 4252, 4253.
   - **1** carries an Opus "Hold the PR until LIN-2995…" follow-up (LIN-4196, root 70e909e8).
   - **3** have no follow-up I could find (LIN-4197, 4198, 4199). All three lineages began before the window; they are unexplained.

   So the observer is billed **inside the work leg** too, not only as `survey-*` legs. "Opus vs Haiku implementation" in `/cost` mostly means "had a Survey after-answer or not". Implementation USD cannot be split into build and after-answer from the wire, because the per-model fold (`byModel`, `cost-read.js:211`) is computed and then dropped (`cost-read.js:472-481`; `routes/proxy-compute.js:744`).
3. **`/cost` carries no tokens.** The fold computes `tokens` (`cost-read.js:205`), but `workerSessions[]` exposes only `rootItemId, kind, dispatchedAt, harness, model, effort, costUsd, durationMs` (`cost-read.js:396`; checked on the wire). "In tokens as well as USD" needs another source (see L5).

### Per-layer audit

**L1 · Cost source: `/api/proxy/issues/{id}/cost`.** Per-lineage USD. A lineage counts once, under the issue of its earliest non-wake member (proxy instructions, `/cost` section). `totalUsd` is null on any unpriced, no-telemetry, unreadable or incomplete lineage (`cost-read.js:445-466`). `durationMs` runs from the fetched base dispatch to lineage completion (`cost-read.js:436-441`): wall time, waiting included, not working time. Worker figures carry no read horizon. App calls read only 30 days (`window.appCallsSince`). Lineages with no request records still read snapshots through the LEGACY reader, deleted no earlier than 2026-12-04 (`cost-read.js:109-111`). **Must hold:** freeze the raw `/cost` JSON with its read time. Pre-records legs are approximate (Haiku unpriced, subagents uncounted); they are not "exact". Never read null as 0.

**L2 · Population (the window).** It cannot be enumerated directly. `GET /dispatch` returns only the 100 newest rows, with no pagination (offset, after, before and page all ignored; tried), and `/issues` carries no dates. Bound used: candidates = every LIN id named in either repo's commits since 2026-11-04T05:00Z (61) ∪ LIN-4170…4257, giving 103. Then per-issue `GET /dispatch?issueIdentifier=` kept those with a row dispatched in the window. **47 tickets** (list in the description). It could miss an older ticket (<LIN-4170) worked in the window that no window commit names. **Rate limit:** 60/min, and 30 of my first 206 calls were 429s. Pace about 1.1 s per call, and check every file for `"error"` before using it.

**L3 · Leg classification (the existing one).** `lib/wall-clock-summary.js:39-59` `BUCKET_OF_KIND` / `bucketOf` (exported) already splits kinds into `before` (plan, plan-review, research, triage, breakdown, spike, bug, blocked, survey-task, survey-place…), `diff` (implementation), `after` (review, close-out, retro, retrospective-audit) and `orchestration` (autopilot, wake, custom, periodical). The ticket's floor/work/keep-alive/survey split re-cuts that table: floor = before (less survey) + after, work = diff, keep-alive = orchestration, survey = survey-* (in `before`). **Must hold:** import `bucketOf` rather than write a fifth kind map, and report survey-* as its own row. Two cases the kind map cannot see:
- (a) the after-answers inside `diff` (correction 2);
- (b) tickets whose `research` leg *is* the work (periodicals: LIN-4206–4209, 4231, 4232, 4249, 4250), plus tickets that landed code with **no implementation lineage**, their work done in autopilot or custom sessions (LIN-4195, 4202, 4219, 4224, 4233; e.g. LIN-4224: $14.05 orchestration, $0 diff). LIN-4201 shows (b) inside a code ticket: 1,006 production lines, $2.24 diff, $30.40 orchestration.

Stratify by ticket type before testing.

**L4 · Size counters (existing).**
- `unwedge-or-breakdown-scripts/sizebands.mjs`: insertions plus deletions of every commit naming a LIN id, all files (tests and docs included), LinearViewer only (repo fixed at `:16`), on HEAD's history despite its rule string saying "all refs" (`:24,43`). Credits a parent every time a child's commit names it: LIN-4195 reads 10,470 lines, LIN-4201 5,238 against 2,626 in its PR. **Sense:** churn by mention. Unfit for per-ticket size in this window except as a stated contrast.
- `coherence-as-it-grows-scripts/coherence-census.mjs prs`: per merged PR, production and test lines and files, plus areas (`:150-191`). **Sense:** landed size (prod lines, files, PRs per ticket) and proving size (test lines). `isProd`/`isTest` (`:25-26`) are LinearViewer paths, so **every one of the 15 simple-dispatcher PRs in the window reads 0/0** (run with `REPO=simple-dispatcher`).
- `scripts/delivery-composition.mjs`: repo-neutral code/test/doc path rule (`:87-89` in the file), but it aggregates **weekly**, not per ticket, and exports nothing. **Sense:** throughput composition. It does not fit as a per-ticket counter. Its path rule is the only existing classifier that works on simple-dispatcher.
- `experiments/place-change/place-change.mjs <repo> <base> <head> scripts/code-shape/areas.json`: the area map at base vs merge (cross-area imports, pairs grown, shrunk, new or closed, files without a home). LinearViewer only (no area guide for simple-dispatcher, `place-ledger.md:8`). Ran clean on LIN-4253's merge (`d9c0f1ca`: 1269→1271 imports, LLM↔Other grew, `lib/stage-writes.js` without a home). **Sense:** one sub-sense of bound size, measurable on *every* LinearViewer merge. That lets the unselected population be compared with the Survey's selected sample.
- Survey prose (`docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md`, `round-2/3/forecasts.md`, `notes-2026-11-05.md`). **Sense:** bound size as judged (copies, carried findings, balance). Covers about 25 of the 47, chosen by the Survey loop, so it is a selected sample. Read it in place.

Band schemes already in the archive, any of which the paper should reuse rather than add a fourth: `how-a-task-is-composed.md:56-58` (2–197 / 201–602 / 613+), `cost-mix.md:242-247` (0 / 1–49 / 50–299 / 300+ production lines), `exposure.py:44` (1-49 / 50-299 / 300+).

*(continued in part 2)*

## Research: LIN-4257, part 2 of 2

**L5 · Tokens.** Not on `/cost` (correction 3). `scripts/survey-costmix-tokens.mjs --since 2026-11-04T05:00:00Z --until … --out …` ran clean on the host's transcripts (229 sessions, 196.8M units, 50 tickets) and gives per-session ticket and kind. Its units are **tier-weighted** (small tier ×0.2, mid ×0.6; `:3-5`), so they are price-shaped and do not settle "within one model". Within-model raw tokens need either `byModel` and `tokens` on `/cost` (a code change; see Surface Assessment) or the Haiku-only stratum.

**L6 · Prior answers to build on, not repeat.**
- `where-the-effort-goes.md:26-28` (Sept, tokens): effort rises with production lines only weakly (ρ 0.19 tokens, 0.21 dispatches, 0.41 hours) and tracks test lines more closely.
- `cost-mix.md:249-255`: a 1–49-line change still costs about 4.2M weighted tokens, and a linear fit puts the intercept at 7.8M of an 8.8M mean. That is the "small-change floor", a lower bound.
- `coherence-as-it-grows.md:100,129` and `the-second-copy.md:139`: no trend in the cost of a same-sized change can be shown.

The new paper's contribution is exact USD per leg on records-era lineages, and whether the floor and the weak slope survive that.

**L7 · Feasibility spike (not a finding).** Single implementation lineage, LinearViewer production lines >0, joined to diff USD:
- **Haiku-labelled:** n=4 (LIN-4203, 4212, 4226, 4247). Too few to compute anything.
- **Opus-labelled** (after-answer folded in): n=10. Spearman ρ(prod lines, diff USD) 0.37, ρ(test lines, diff USD) 0.47, ρ(prod lines, floor USD) 0.36.

Same direction as L6. The test is feasible, but at this n it is descriptive, not a rate. The population grows by roughly 30 tickets a day.

**L8 · Natural experiments, re-read 11:5x on 5 Nov.**
| Ticket | State | `/cost` |
|---|---|---|
| LIN-4253 | Done | total $11.24 |
| LIN-4251 | **In Progress** | total null, `noTelemetryCount: 1` |
| LIN-4252 | Done | total $10.38 |
| LIN-4246 | **In Progress** | total null, `noTelemetryCount: 1`; no close-out; surveyed twice |
| LIN-4255 | Backlog | `noLineage: true` (unknown, not $0) |
| LIN-4254 | Backlog | `noLineage: true` (a second tidy-after of the fake DOM, not named in the ticket) |
| LIN-4247 (control) | Done | total $6.27; survey legs $1.85 |
| LIN-4201 | Done | total $40.13 |
| LIN-4226 | Done | total $27.84 |

Both pairs are still incomplete, and each is n=1.

**L9 · Library obligations.**
- `docs/papers/README.md`: a scan of every `harbour/*.md` against the index finds **exactly two** missing: `fleet-complexity-read` (no `kind:`, so a paper by default) and `replay-small-work-preregistration` (`kind: pre-registration`, a kind `standard.md` does not define; index it beside `replay-small-work`). The set is closed by that scan.
- `proposals.md:81-86` asks for runner working hours per same-sized change by month since June against exposure. `/cost` cannot reach June. Answer the same-sized-change half for the exact window and rewrite the line to the part that stays open (the trend: runner hours from June, or `/cost` re-read monthly from 4 Nov). Rewrite it, don't add a second line. `standard.md` rule 3: Next feeds `proposals.md` in the same PR.

### Attack on this audit
- **Missed sibling counters?** I searched `scripts/` for size, cost, survey and place names, and the paper scripts for `prodLines|production lines`. Results: `survey-effort-git.mjs`, `survey-model-git.mjs` and `survey-growth-git.mjs` exist and also count lines (cost-mix's `isProd` says it follows `steady-base-code.mjs` and `survey-growth-git.mjs`), so the "production line" rule already has at least three copies. That is the Survey's point that "size has no single home". I did not read those three in full. The paper should name them and use `coherence-census.mjs` for comparability with the 229/45 figure.
- **Population miss:** it could hold an old ticket worked in the window but never named in a window commit. The paper should state the bound.
- **Unexplained:** three Opus-labelled implementation lineages (LIN-4197, 4198, 4199) have no follow-up I found.

### Surface Assessment
`Surface Assessment: [improvement noticed, not required: put each lineage's existing per-model fold and tokens (byModel/tokens, already computed at lib/cost-read.js:205,211) on the /cost wire (cost-read.js:472-481, routes/proxy-compute.js:744, proxy-instructions /cost entry), as its own small ticket — the paper is read-only by the person's scope and works around it by stratifying]`

The paper itself lands cleanly: one new document, a dated evidence folder beside it, a README edit and a proposals edit. It needs no new model of size or cost, provided it imports `bucketOf` and invokes the existing counters. One inline edit is needed: export `delivery-composition.mjs`'s path predicates (with a main guard, no behaviour change) so simple-dispatcher PRs get production and test lines without a new counter. That changes an analysis script, not product code.

**One question for John.** Should the `/cost` per-model and tokens exposure land *before* the paper, so the within-model test is exact? Or should the paper go ahead read-only now, using the Haiku-only stratum and weighted units, and name the exposure in Next? **Recommendation: go ahead now, and file the exposure as its own ticket.** The window is thin anyway, so a v2 after about two weeks of records, with `byModel`, is where a within-model rate becomes possible.

Write the paper now, read-only; file the /cost change as its own ticket

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## LIN-4257: implementation done, PR open

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2294 (branch `feat/lin-4257-task-size-and-cost`, commit 783a0575). CI is green: unit tests, secret scan, and all four E2E shards.

**The answer, in short.** On 22 tickets with exact cost in the first 31 hours of `/cost` records, the floor (planning, plan-review, review, close-out) has a median share of 44% and rises with landed lines (ρ 0.71 against LinearViewer production lines, n=22). The implementation leg does not follow production lines in the Opus-labelled group with a Survey after-answer (ρ −0.01, n=10). The Haiku-only clean stratum has n=4, so it reports no coefficient. The two repositories disagree in sign against the floor, so they are not pooled.

**What is in the PR.** The paper `docs/papers/harbour/task-size-and-cost.md` (kind: paper, version 1). Frozen evidence and re-run commands in `docs/papers/harbour/task-size-and-cost-evidence/2026-11-05/`. Scripts in `docs/papers/harbour/task-size-and-cost-scripts/`. Index rows for the paper and the two papers the index was missing. The same-sized-change line in `proposals.md` rewritten to the trend half. `scripts/delivery-paths.mjs` extracted from `delivery-composition.mjs` (output byte-identical before and after).

**Still open.** A fresh-reader review before merge (the ticket's Done-when). The per-model fold and tokens on `/cost` are not yet filed as their own ticket. A version 2 re-freeze is due around 19 November.

## Review — LIN-4257

Reviewed PR [LinearViewer #2294](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2294) at head `783a0575d61995c3ef556eed10e49c153515f7a3` (branch `feat/lin-4257-task-size-and-cost`, base `main` at `2f0c9d5b`).

## The ruling's two parts, and one finding for PR #2294's review

**Where the ruling landed** ("Write the paper now, read-only; file the /cost change as its own ticket", 12:31):
- **Paper:** PR #2294 (`feat/lin-4257-task-size-and-cost`), from the pipeline's implementation. CI is green. I didn't open a second paper PR. A parallel draft I had started was deleted unpushed; its 12:45 freeze is kept below only as a cross-check.
- **/cost change:** this already exists as **LIN-4263** (filed 12:21, In Progress), so the close-out's "not yet filed" is out of date. I filed LIN-4264 at 12:31 without seeing it, and have closed it as a Duplicate of LIN-4263.

**Finding: the paper's "clean" stratum depends on when it was read.** PR #2294's freeze finished at `2026-11-05T12:15:59Z` (`task-size-and-cost-evidence/2026-11-05/manifest.json`). Two of its four clean tickets later gained an Opus Survey after-answer inside their implementation lineage. A second read of `/cost` and `/dispatch/{id}`, at 12:33–12:45, shows:

| Ticket | After-answer dispatched | Implementation USD in #2294 | At 12:45 | `/cost` label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIN-4247 | `daf89966`, 12:21:44 | $0.70 | **$2.34** (+$1.64) | Haiku → **Opus** |
| LIN-4251 | `5143f6b8`, 12:21:43 | $1.59 | **$4.13** (+$2.54) | Haiku → **Opus** |
| LIN-4203 | none | $2.55 | $2.55 | Haiku |
| LIN-4212 | none (three Haiku implementation follow-ups, 4 Nov) | $2.87 | $2.87 | Haiku |

Two consequences for the paper:
1. **"Clean" means "read before its after-answer was sent", not "never observed".** A finished ticket's work leg isn't final until the Survey has sent its after-answer, which here came about 1–1.5 h after merge. The paper should say this in Method and Limits. Alternatively it can define "clean" as "no Survey after-answer sent *or due*". Re-freezing would leave the clean stratum at n=2.
2. **It is also the only direct measure of the observer billed inside the work leg.** On these two tickets the after-answer cost more than the Haiku build itself: +$1.64 against $0.70, and +$2.54 against $1.59. That is n=2, an anecdote, but it is the size of what LIN-4263 will make visible. It belongs beside the paper's "work+observer" group (ρ −0.01, n=10): that group's implementation USD may be mostly after-answer, which would explain why it doesn't follow production lines.

These are re-reads of live `/cost` and `/dispatch/{id}`, not edits; nothing in code, tickets or rulings was changed to produce them. The raw 12:45 freeze sits in my session scratchpad, not in the repo. If the paper uses the two deltas, it should make its own dated re-read.
